ns2:section.sectionText: In this course, we will survey major developments in the history of thinking hard from the eighteenth century to today. To cope with the unwieldy and sometimes stupefying abstraction called ”critical theory,” we will generally read short, iconic selections, thinking for the most part in broad, vivid strokes, with a few full texts interspersed for depth and texture. Most importantly (for newcomers to such material), we will work through these readings in a way that makes sense, challenges you, and does not put any of us to sleep (or drive us crazy). This is, in short, an introduction to the history of Big Ideas, and any lively, alert, thinking reader should be able to keep up. A large part of this class is about what theory says. But an even bigger part is simply about learning how to read theory. And we will do that by doing what we do in every English class: close reading the text itself.
